calls.reason: NVIDIA's 10-Q shows its revenue is concentrated, and Meta cites its own AI uses as a reason to buy. Nothing here shows that buyers' plans depend mainly on the two labs spending over $400B, so the causal claim cannot be called.
Meta's 10-Q shows small AI-glasses sales growth, and its July call mentions a newly launched priced model API. Neither is sized, and 'really' has no threshold, so the evidence is mixed.

NVIDIA's filings give no customer counts. Comparing like with like, the top three customers' share of receivables fell from 64% in Q1 to 49% in Q2, which undercuts the concentration evidence the contraction claim rests on.

CNBC repeated the figure without giving a base period, and TechCrunch gave a generic definition plus a caveat that methods may differ. Two articles are too thin a sample to judge the sweeping claim about uncritical coverage.
The test runs to September 2028. Hut 8 targets first Beacon Point data-hall delivery in Q3 2027, and October reporting still describes construction, so the outcome is not decided.

Anthropic's S-1 shows about $131B in June working capital and positive adjusted income, and OpenAI raised $122B in committed capital. But commitment totals are left blank, so no matched payment schedule settles whether they can afford it.
